title: When Texas Bat “Cities” Look Like Thunderstorms - Nautilus
gist: Bracken Cave in Texas hosts up to nearly 20 million free-tailed bats each summer, the largest congregation of nonhuman mammals on Earth, whose nightly emergence is dense enough to look like storms on Doppler radar. The colony eats more than 150 tons of insects a night, prompting weather apps to filter such scenes out by default.

insights.claim: For at least 8,500 years, Texas' Bracken Cave has filled each spring with up to 10 million free-tailed bats migrating about 700 miles north from roosts in and around central Mexico.
insights.speaker: Ryan Huling
insights.so_what: Illustrates a long-stable ecological system with migration across the US-Mexico border.

insights.claim: After pups are born the Bracken Cave population doubles to nearly 20 million, the largest congregation of nonhuman mammals on Earth.
insights.speaker: Ryan Huling
insights.so_what: A unique natural asset with ecotourism and conservation significance.
insights.quote: the population will double again to nearly 20 million—the largest congregation of nonhuman mammals on Earth

insights.claim: At peak population it takes over three and a half hours for every bat to exit the cave's bottleneck entrance during the nightly 'emergence.'
insights.speaker: Ryan Huling
insights.so_what: Quantifies the scale of the phenomenon.

insights.claim: The bats fly up to 10,000 feet, travel 60 to 100 miles a night, and collectively eat more than 150 tons of moths, beetles and other insects nightly.
insights.speaker: Ryan Huling
insights.so_what: Implies substantial natural pest control for surrounding agricultural fields.
insights.quote: collectively consuming more than 150 tons of moths, beetles, and other insects

insights.claim: Because bat emergences resemble thunderstorms on Doppler radar, weather apps generally modify default settings to remove such scenes so viewers do not think a downpour is imminent.
insights.speaker: Ryan Huling
insights.so_what: Biological clutter is a real data-quality issue for weather radar products and their filtering algorithms.
insights.quote: Weather apps generally modify their default settings to remove such scenes from Doppler radarviews.
